plan.title: Kidney aldosterone vs vehicle DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a single-batch, unpaired 6-vs-6 human kidney bulk RNA-seq comparison (aldosterone-treated vs vehicle), gene-level counts from Salmon with 12,000 genes x 12 samples, delivered without stated length correction. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure: (1) sample-structure QC to confirm the treated/control split is the dominant axis of variance before any test runs and to catch outliers, since a 6-vs-6 design has little slack for a mislabeled or aberrant sample; (2) minimal count pre-filtering, median-of-ratios normalization inside DESeq2, and a Wald test with an explicit reference level (vehicle) and a named contrast (aldosterone vs vehicle), because the counts are gene-level from Salmon with no per-sample quantification files or transcript-length table delivered, so the length offset cannot be reconstructed and the model runs on the counts as delivered — this is stated as a caveat, not silently absorbed; (3) apeglm shrinkage of the fold change for ranking and reporting, BH-adjusted significance at the standard 0.05 threshold with DESeq2's independent filtering kept on, answering 'which genes change'; (4) preranked fgsea on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (human, 2026.1) to place the DE genes in known biological programs; (5) decoupleR univariate linear model TF-activity inference on the same Wald statistic using the CollecTRI human regulon network, answering 'which transcription factors sit behind those changes' from the full ranked list rather than a thresholded gene list, per the grounded rule that a small unpaired design cannot support a data-driven regulatory network (ARACNe/VIPER) and must use a curated prior network instead; (6) an integrated report tying the top six up- and top six down-regulated genes and the top TF activities together with all required diagnostics, thresholds, and reproducibility metadata. All steps are grounded in the cited DESeq2/apeglm/fgsea/decoupleR literature and checked against the knowledge service's method-permission rules.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
